The claim states that at higher concurrencies, the interaction between decomposition geometry and camera direction causes the hybrid-memory implementation to underperform distributed memory by 10% due to irregular block sizes in GPU clusters. It further explains that this effect is caused by 'the difference in decomposition geometries' and notes that 'the smaller size of the GPU cluster limited the concurrencies we could choose for the hybrid/CUDA implementation, leading to similarly irregular blocks in that case.' The mention of 'camera direction' in the claim aligns with the source's discussion that 'The interaction of the decomposition geometry and the camera direction determines the maximum number of ray integration steps' and that performance depends on 'the view.' Thus, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
